items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: He used to come and sit on the music stand where we'd be at playing.

ctx.x: You see Papa Lane. Do you remember Jack Lane by any chance? The white drummer who had a lot of bands here?

No. The ones that I know came up under us was, what do you call him? Oh they got a six piece band there. He's a trumpet player. Nickle Rock? No. He kind of buzzed off. He learned under Kid Rene. This fellow. Sharky? Sharky. Sharky Banana. That's the one. Now you see he's got all those Dixieland style like Rene play. Because he learned, he plays trumpet on the style of Rene too. Because he learned right from Rene. Got all the finger from Rene. He used to come and sit on the music stand where we'd be at playing.…

He got a little jazz from Rene. Yeah. That's where he got it from. And I was telling Mr. Russell, you remember after Rene was kind of going down. I had to play this jippie dance. His wife. She live in Rapshap. Yeah. She calls me and says take Henry to learn the music without checking. Yeah. When him and son used to come over. Yeah son Thomas. Yeah. Fan joke there. Uh huh. And I start him off that he could read his reviews. Yeah. That's right. That's right. And the same time then Joe got interested. He never could…
